title: The Thief's Beard Grows - Most famous (Español)
summary: Birbal uses the famous folk belief of growing beards to trap an elusive burglar who robbed the imperial jewelers. [ES]
keywords: the thief's beard grows - most famous
full_text:
A daring burglar broke into the workshop of the master imperial goldsmith in Agra, escaping with half a chest of uncut emeralds. The police caught three notorious fences who had been seen near the shop, but all three vehemently denied any involvement in the burglary.

Brought before Emperor Akbar, the suspects wept and claimed they were harmless merchants.

Akbar summoned Birbal to untangle the mystery. Birbal had the three men placed in separate cells for the night. Next morning, Birbal stood before the prisoners and announced with solemn gravity:

'I have sprinkled sacred water from the Ganges upon your cells last night. An ancient blessing has taken root: by noon today, the beard of the true thief will grow longer by the width of four fingers through celestial power, while the beards of the innocent will remain untouched!'

Two of the suspects laughed, knowing such a thing was physically impossible.

However, the actual thief was terrified. When left alone in his cell, he took a pair of small trimming scissors from his pouch and frantically snipped off four fingers' length from his beard, muttering: 'Now, when the magic makes it grow four fingers longer, it will match its original size and fool the minister!'

At noon, Birbal lined up the three men. Two had normal beards, but the third man's beard was freshly hacked, uneven, and noticeably shorter!

'Arrest him!' Birbal commanded. 'His own scissors have signed his confession!'

The thief broke down and led guards to the hidden emeralds. Akbar marveled at how superstition had once again delivered justice into Birbal's hands.
